newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian senator Colston asked to quit key post.
newsitem.headline: Australian senator Colston asked to quit key post.

text.p: Australian Senate President Margaret Reid said on Thursday she had asked key independent senator Mal Colston, accused of abusing allowances, to stand aside as deputy president of parliament's upper house.
But Reid said Colston had not indicated what he would do.
"(I) stated (my) view to Senator Colston that it would be appropriate for him to stand down as deputy president of the Senate at this stage," Reid said in a statement.
"Senator Colston noted (my) views. He gave no indication of his intended course of action."
Reid said Colston had contacted her late on Wednesday afternoon after promising last week to discuss his future with her this week.
The Labor opposition and other Senate parties have also demanded Colston stand aside as deputy president and quit the Senate because of police investigations into fraud allegations.

Colston, an independent who defected from Labor in August last year and whose vote is crucial to the passage of government legislation, was released from a Brisbane hospital last week after suffering an undisclosed medical condition.
He is currently convalescing in an unknown location.

The government has rejected calls for a Senate inquiry into allegations that Colston misled the upper house over errors in his travel allowance claims, but has said it would no longer accept his vote.
